## Setup

This analysis uses the combined weekly-scores dataset (seasons 1-34), scraped
from Wikipedia. We restrict to rows that:

- Have a matched celebrity **and** professional (a small number of couples
  could not be reliably matched back to the cast table and are dropped).
- Are **not** team/group dances (relays, marathons, "Team" theme dances,
  season finale trios, etc.) — we're only interested in a single celebrity/pro
  couple's individual performance.
- Have a single, well-formed dance style (a handful of rows list two dances
  or a swapped mid-season partner and are dropped rather than guessed at).

Because the number of judges scoring a routine varies across the show's
history (3 judges most seasons, 4 in others, occasionally more), we compare
routines using the **average score per judge** rather than the raw total, so
scores are on a comparable ~0-10 scale throughout.

```{python}
import re

import polars as pl
from plotnine import *

df = pl.read_parquet("../data/dwts_all_seasons.parquet")

# team/group/relay/marathon-style dances and other malformed multi-dance
# entries we don't want mixed in with individual couple performances
TEAM_DANCE_PATTERN = r"(?i)team|group|relay|marathon|megamix|&|\(|\)"

clean = (
    df.with_columns(
        pl.col("judge_scores").list.len().alias("n_judges"),
    )
    .filter(
        pl.col("is_group_dance").not_(),
        pl.col("celebrity").is_not_null(),
        pl.col("professional").is_not_null(),
        pl.col("professional").str.contains(r"\(").not_(),  # mid-season partner swaps
        pl.col("dance").is_not_null(),
        pl.col("dance").str.contains(TEAM_DANCE_PATTERN).not_(),
        pl.col("total_score").is_not_null(),
        pl.col("score_type").is_null(),  # technical/performance split weeks
        pl.col("n_judges").is_not_null(),
    )
    .with_columns((pl.col("total_score") / pl.col("n_judges")).alias("avg_judge_score"))
)

print(f"{df.height} total rows -> {clean.height} individual-couple rows kept")
```

## Which pros score the highest?

For each professional dancer, we compute their average per-judge score across
every individual routine in the dataset. To avoid ranking pros who only
danced a handful of times, we require at least 15 qualifying routines.

```{python}
MIN_DANCES = 15

pro_summary = (
    clean.group_by("professional")
    .agg(
        pl.len().alias("n_dances"),
        pl.col("avg_judge_score").mean().alias("mean_score"),
        pl.col("avg_judge_score").std().alias("sd_score"),
    )
    .filter(pl.col("n_dances") >= MIN_DANCES)
)

top_scoring_pros = pro_summary.sort("mean_score", descending=True).head(15)
top_scoring_pros
```

```{python}
p = (
    ggplot(
        top_scoring_pros,
        aes(x="reorder(professional, mean_score)", y="mean_score"),
    )
    + geom_col(fill="#c94277")
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(
        title="Highest-scoring professionals (avg. score per judge)",
        subtitle=f"Individual couple dances only, min. {MIN_DANCES} routines",
        x="",
        y="Average score per judge",
    )
    + theme_minimal()
)

p
```

## Which pros are the most consistent?

"Consistent" here means a low standard deviation in per-judge score across
all of a pro's routines — i.e. they don't swing between very high and very
low scores from week to week. This is a different question from who scores
highest on average; a pro could be consistently mediocre or consistently
excellent.

```{python}
most_consistent_pros = pro_summary.sort("sd_score").head(15)
most_consistent_pros
```

```{python}
p = (
    ggplot(pro_summary, aes(x="mean_score", y="sd_score"))
    + geom_point(alpha=0.6, size=2)
    + labs(
        title="Average score vs. consistency by professional",
        subtitle=f"Individual couple dances only, min. {MIN_DANCES} routines",
        x="Average score per judge",
        y="Standard deviation of score per judge (lower = more consistent)",
    )
    + theme_minimal()
)

p
```

Note the mild tradeoff visible above: pros with higher average scores also
tend to have somewhat lower variance, which makes sense if stronger dancers
are less likely to have a truly bad week.

## Which dance styles score the highest?

Now looking at dance style rather than pro: does the show's panel score some
dance styles more generously than others? Again using average score per
judge, and again restricted to individual (non-team) couple performances.

```{python}
MIN_DANCE_COUNT = 10

dance_summary = (
    clean.group_by("dance")
    .agg(
        pl.len().alias("n_routines"),
        pl.col("avg_judge_score").mean().alias("mean_score"),
        pl.col("avg_judge_score").std().alias("sd_score"),
    )
    .filter(pl.col("n_routines") >= MIN_DANCE_COUNT)
    .sort("mean_score", descending=True)
)

dance_summary
```

```{python}
p = (
    ggplot(
        dance_summary,
        aes(x="reorder(dance, mean_score)", y="mean_score"),
    )
    + geom_col(fill="#3b7dd8")
    + coord_flip()
    + labs(
        title="Average score per judge by dance style",
        subtitle=f"Individual couple dances only, min. {MIN_DANCE_COUNT} routines",
        x="",
        y="Average score per judge",
    )
    + theme_minimal()
)

p
```
